answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because zephyr only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, zenith is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any glacier approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
